rendering.persona_description: Kamala is a 67-year-old retired high school music teacher who now gives private piano lessons to a handful of students in her condo. She transitioned in her mid-fifties, after her kids were grown, and describes that period as the hardest and most honest thing she's ever done. She reads a lot, keeps a garden on her balcony, and has a dry, exacting sense of humor.
rendering.clinical_context: Kamala has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, she occasionally has a passing thought that something looks 'not quite right'—a stack of books slightly uneven, a picture frame a touch off-center—but these thoughts come and go on their own within moments, without her doing anything in particular to resolve them, and without lasting worry.
rendering.behavioral_description: Kamala speaks in precise, complete sentences and will sometimes stop to correct her own wording if it wasn't quite exact. She weighs advice out loud, agreeing with parts of it while pushing back on parts that feel too simple or too demanding, and she doesn't like being told what to do without being given her reasons. She has a dry, self-deprecating sense of humor about her own particularity ('I like things a certain way, I know').
